newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Nationalist parties lead Bosnia parliamentary race.
newsitem.headline: Nationalist parties lead Bosnia parliamentary race.

text.p: The same Serb, Croat and Moslem nationalist parties that helped ignite the war in Bosnia were leading in the country's parliamentary elections, international organisers said on Wednesday.

The Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA), the hardline Serb Democratic Party (SDS) and the Croat Democratic Union (HDZ) were ahead in the race for the 42-member joint House of Representatives, organisers reported in Sarajevo.
The House of Representatives is to rule over a union of Serb and Moslem-Croat entities along with an upper chamber, the House of Peoples, which is appointed by regional assemblies.
One third of the seats are elected from the Serb republic, the remainder from the Moslem-Croat federation.

The SDA had 542,400 votes, or 56 percent and the HDZ had 203,947 votes, or 21 percent in the Moslem-Croat Federation. The SDS won in the Serb republic with 209,289 votes or 66 percent of the vote, the OSCE reported.
The results were based on votes from 64 out of 79 counting centres in federation territory and 36 out of 72 centres in the Serb republic.
